summary: Learn feature flag governance, progressive delivery, observability, and experimentation controls. Build practical release artefacts. Enrol today.
lede: Governed feature flagging and experimentation training helps teams control how changes are exposed, paused, rolled back, and removed throughout the software delivery lifecycle. It covers flag classification, ownership, release-risk assessment, progressive rollouts, telemetry requirements, experiment guardrails, and decision records. You will practise building flag registers, approval paths, canary and dark-launch runbooks, telemetry plans, and experiment scorecards using OpenFeature, OpenTelemetry, and risk-based release practices. The course also examines operational patterns for LaunchDarkly, Unleash, and Flagsmith, with a focus on governance artefacts, observability evidence, incident response, and stakeholder reporting rather than production platform deployment.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who govern or execute production change through feature flags, progressive delivery, and experimentation platforms. It suits intermediate practitioners who can work with software delivery concepts and need a stronger risk, observability, and communication model.
prerequisites: You should have working knowledge of software delivery, CI/CD pipelines, cloud or application operations, and production change processes. Experience with feature flags, observability, incident management, or experimentation is useful but not required. No programming is required for completion. Exercises use architecture diagrams, configuration examples, dashboards, registers, and decision templates rather than production code. Advanced topics such as experiment statistics, AI-assisted release analysis, and platform integration are taught at conceptual and operational application level, not production engineering level.
